messages.content:
Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

Now perform the same with the following input
input: {
    "question": "user: What are the security implications of configuring non-HTTP/HTTPS traffic for global load balancers?\nassistant:  I don't have specific information on the security implications of configuring non-HTTP/HTTPS traffic for global load balancers.\nuser: What exactly the global load balancers do and any subscription  available?\nassistant: Global load balancers help distribute network or application traffic across multiple locations or regions. IBM Cloud Internet Services (CIS) is an example of a global load balancer provider, offering features like Global Load Balancer (GLB), Caching, Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Page rules. They help to ensure reliability and performance by directing traffic to the most available and responsive endpoints. As for subscriptions, IBM CIS offers various plans, including a Free Trial plan with limited features and Standard paid plans with additional capabilities. You can refer to the IBM Cloud website for the most current and detailed information on their subscription options.\n\nuser: How frequently do you do a health check in the back-end? and is there any limitations?\nassistant: Health checks in IBM Cloud Internet Services (CIS) are done periodically to monitor the availability of origin servers. The frequency of these health checks is every 15 seconds. However, the default retry rate is 5 retries per second, which can be configured. It is not recommended to increase the retry rate significantly as retries use exponential backoff.\nRegarding limitations, it is important to note that health checks for deleted pools and origins cannot be filtered, but they still appear in the table. Also, when adding the request header name for a health check, use 'Host' with a capitalized 'H'. Using a lower-case 'host' for a health check will fail.\n\nuser: how do you distribute among bare-metal and virtual-server instances?  Multiple policies ok?\nassistant: The IBM Cloud Load Balancer service distributes traffic among multiple server instances, including bare-metal and virtual-server instances, by using Layer 7 (application layer) data. Layer 7 load balancing is supported for HTTP and HTTPS traffic only. Multiple policies can be associated with a front-end port, and these policies are evaluated in order, based on the priority assigned to each policy. Each Layer 7 rule is associated with a policy, and if all the rules that are associated with the policy evaluate to true, the policy is matched, so the associated action is taken.\nFor more information, see [L7 Policy and Rules](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/loadbalancer-service?topic=loadbalancer-service-layer-7-policy).\n\nuser: If not, what wd happen?\nassistant: If you refer to the scenario where multiple policies are not associated with a front-end port in the IBM Cloud Load Balancer service, then the system might not be able to apply the appropriate actions to the data traffic. \nuser: Then do I lose all the traffic?  any remedy?",
    "answer": "不会必然丢失流量。若请求不匹配任何策略的规则，HTTP 监听器会优先将请求重定向到已配置的 HTTPS 重定向监听器；若未配置，则转发到该监听器的默认池。可配置 HTTPS 重定向监听器或默认池作为处理路径。策略只有在其所有规则都匹配时才会应用。根据第1页。"
}
Output:

response_text:
{
  "statements": [
    "在 IBM Cloud Load Balancer 服务中，请求未匹配任何策略的规则并不必然导致流量丢失。",
    "当请求未匹配任何策略的规则且已配置 HTTPS 重定向监听器时，HTTP 监听器会优先将请求重定向到已配置的 HTTPS 重定向监听器。",
    "当请求未匹配任何策略的规则且未配置 HTTPS 重定向监听器时，HTTP 监听器会将请求转发到 HTTP 监听器的默认池。",
    "可以配置 HTTPS 重定向监听器，作为未匹配任何策略规则的请求的处理路径。",
    "可以配置默认池，作为未匹配任何策略规则且未配置 HTTPS 重定向监听器时的请求处理路径。",
    "只有策略关联的全部规则都匹配请求时，策略才会应用。",
    "上述负载均衡处理说明依据第1页。"
  ]
}

statements: 在 IBM Cloud Load Balancer 服务中，请求未匹配任何策略的规则并不必然导致流量丢失。
当请求未匹配任何策略的规则且已配置 HTTPS 重定向监听器时，HTTP 监听器会优先将请求重定向到已配置的 HTTPS 重定向监听器。
当请求未匹配任何策略的规则且未配置 HTTPS 重定向监听器时，HTTP 监听器会将请求转发到 HTTP 监听器的默认池。
可以配置 HTTPS 重定向监听器，作为未匹配任何策略规则的请求的处理路径。
可以配置默认池，作为未匹配任何策略规则且未配置 HTTPS 重定向监听器时的请求处理路径。
只有策略关联的全部规则都匹配请求时，策略才会应用。
上述负载均衡处理说明依据第1页。
